text: The process of recording business transactions in the books of accounts is called
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Book keeping is the systematic recording of financial transactions.

text: Which accounting principle says revenue should be recorded when it is earned not when cash is received
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: The accrual concept records revenue and expenses when they occur regardless of cash flow.

text: The accounting equation is expressed as Assets equals Liabilities plus
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Assets equal liabilities plus owners equity or capital.

text: The convention of conservatism means anticipate no profit but provide for all possible losses
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Conservatism guides accountants to be cautious and not overstate income or assets.

text: State any four users of accounting information
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Owners investors creditors managers government and employees.
explanation: Each user needs accounting information for different decisions.

text: Explain the going concern concept and its significance
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: The going concern concept assumes the business will continue for the foreseeable future. Assets are therefore valued at cost and not at liquidation value and expenses are allocated over periods.
explanation: This assumption underlies depreciation and the classification of assets and liabilities.

text: A business has total assets of 500000 and liabilities of 200000. The capital of the owner is
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Capital equals assets minus liabilities so 500000 minus 200000 equals 300000.

text: Which book is the first and original record where transactions are first entered
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: The journal is the book of original entry where transactions are first recorded.

text: The account that is debited when goods are purchased for cash is
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Purchases are debited and cash is credited when goods are bought for cash.

text: The golden rule for personal accounts is debit the receiver and credit the
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Personal accounts follow the rule debit the receiver credit the giver.

text: A trial balance is a statement that verifies the arithmetical accuracy of ledger balances
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: A trial balance checks that total debits equal total credits.

text: Pass the journal entry for goods sold on credit to Ravi for 10000
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Debit Ravi account 10000 and credit Sales account 10000.
explanation: Ravi is the receiver so he is debited and sales is a nominal gain so it is credited.

text: Explain the objectives of preparing a trial balance
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: A trial balance checks arithmetical accuracy of postings and helps locate errors. It provides the balances needed to prepare final accounts and gives a summary of all ledger accounts.
explanation: Note that a tallied trial balance does not guarantee that no errors exist.

text: A firm purchased goods for 25000 and paid carriage of 1000 in cash. The total amount to be debited to purchases is
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Carriage inward is debited separately to carriage account not to purchases unless the question specifies otherwise.

text: The cash book which has both cash and bank columns on each side is called a
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Two column cash book|Petty cash book|Sales book|Purchases book
explanation: A two column cash book records cash and bank transactions side by side.

text: Credit sales are recorded in which subsidiary book
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Credit sales go in the sales book while cash sales go in the cash book.

text: The petty cash book is maintained under which system
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Under the imprest system a fixed amount is given to the petty cashier and reimbursed periodically.

text: Cash sales of 5000 should be entered in the sales book
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Only credit sales go in the sales book; cash sales are recorded in the cash book.

text: Distinguish between a cash book and a pass book
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: A cash book is maintained by the business and records its own cash and bank dealings. A pass book is kept by the bank and shows the same transactions from the banks point of view.
explanation: The same transaction appears on opposite sides of the two books.

text: Explain the advantages of maintaining subsidiary books
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Subsidiary books divide the journal so similar transactions are recorded together. They save time allow division of work and make information easy to find and post to the ledger.
explanation: Cover division of work specialisation and ease of posting.

text: A trader received cash 6000 and allowed discount 200. The amount debited to discount allowed is
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Discount allowed is a loss to the business and is debited at the amount of the discount given.

text: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared mainly to
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Reconcile the cash book and pass book balances|Prepare final accounts|Record credit sales|Calculate depreciation
explanation: A BRS explains the difference between the bank balance in the cash book and the pass book.

text: Cheques issued but not yet presented for payment cause the cash book balance to be
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Higher than the pass book|Lower than the pass book|Equal to the pass book|Unchanged
explanation: Such cheques are already reduced in the cash book but not yet in the pass book so the cash book balance is lower.

text: Bank charges debited by the bank appear only in the pass book and reduce the balance
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Bank charges are recorded by the bank first and lower the pass book balance until entered in the cash book.

text: List any four causes of difference between the cash book and pass book balances
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Cheques issued but not presented cheques deposited but not credited bank charges and interest allowed by the bank are common causes.
explanation: Timing differences and bank entries unknown to the business cause the gap.

text: Explain the need for preparing a bank reconciliation statement
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: A BRS reconciles the two balances so errors and fraud can be detected and delayed items identified. It gives the true bank balance and helps in cash management.
explanation: Cover detection of errors prevention of fraud and correct cash position.

text: The cash book shows a bank balance of 8000. A cheque of 2000 issued is not yet presented. The balance as per pass book will be
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: An unpresented cheque means the pass book still shows the amount so add 2000 to 8000 giving 10000.

text: The final account that shows the financial position of a business on a date is the
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Balance sheet|Trading account|Profit and loss account|Trial balance
explanation: The balance sheet is a statement of assets and liabilities on a particular date.

text: Closing stock appears in which accounts of the final statements
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Trading account and balance sheet|Only trading account|Only balance sheet|Profit and loss account
explanation: Closing stock is credited to the trading account and shown as a current asset in the balance sheet.

text: Outstanding expenses are shown in the balance sheet as a
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Outstanding expenses are amounts due but unpaid so they are a current liability.

text: Carriage inward is shown on the debit side of the trading account
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Carriage inward is a direct expense on purchases so it is debited to the trading account.

text: Explain the difference between capital expenditure and revenue expenditure
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Capital expenditure gives benefit over many years and is shown as an asset. Revenue expenditure benefits only the current period and is charged to the profit and loss account.
explanation: The distinction rests on the period of benefit derived from the spending.

text: Describe the adjustments required before preparing final accounts
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Key adjustments include closing stock outstanding and prepaid expenses accrued and unearned income depreciation bad debts and provision for doubtful debts. Each adjustment has a dual effect on trading P and L and the balance sheet.
explanation: Explain the dual aspect of each adjustment with its placement.

text: Gross profit is 40000 and operating expenses are 15000. The net profit is
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Net profit equals gross profit minus operating expenses so 40000 minus 15000 equals 25000.

text: The amount charged to the profit and loss account each year for the use of a fixed asset is called
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Depreciation allocates the cost of a fixed asset over its useful life.

text: Under the straight line method depreciation is calculated on the
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Straight line depreciation charges a fixed percentage on the original cost each year.

text: The written down value method of depreciation charges a higher amount in the early years
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: The WDV method applies a fixed rate to the reducing balance so depreciation is higher in early years.

text: The system of accounting that ignores the double entry principle and keeps incomplete records is called
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Single entry keeps only personal and cash accounts and no complete double entry record.

text: State the methods of calculating depreciation
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: The main methods are straight line method written down value method and annuity and machine hour methods.
explanation: Straight line and WDV are the two most common methods.

text: Explain the causes of depreciation of fixed assets
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Depreciation arises from wear and tear from use passage of time obsolescence due to new technology and depletion of natural resources. It matches the cost of the asset with the revenue it earns.
explanation: Cover physical deterioration obsolescence and the matching principle.

text: A machine costs 100000 with scrap value 10000 and useful life ten years. Annual depreciation under straight line method is
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Depreciation equals cost minus scrap divided by life so 90000 divided by 10 equals 9000.

text: Which account is credited when a cheque received from a customer is deposited in the bank
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: The customer account is credited and the bank account is debited when a cheque is banked.

text: Assertion: A trial balance that agrees is proof that no errors exist. Reason: Some errors do not affect the equality of debits and credits
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Assertion is false but reason is true|Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion|Both are true but reason does not explain assertion|Assertion is true but reason is false
explanation: Errors of omission and compensating errors do not disturb the trial balance so a tallied trial balance is not conclusive proof.

text: Match the book to its content
subject: Financial Accounting
options: Sales book - credit sales|Purchases book - cash sales|Cash book - credit purchases|Journal proper - petty expenses
explanation: The sales book records credit sales while the cash book records cash transactions.

text: Read the case: A firm paid 12000 as insurance premium for the year. Only 3000 relates to the current period. Identify the amount to be charged to the profit and loss account and the amount to be shown as an asset
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: 3000 is charged to the profit and loss account as insurance expense and 9000 is shown as prepaid insurance under current assets.
explanation: Only the current years portion is an expense and the balance is prepaid.

text: Read the case: The cash book shows an overdraft of 5000. A cheque of 1500 deposited is not yet credited by the bank. Calculate the balance as per the pass book and state whether it is an overdraft
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: The pass book shows a larger overdraft of 6500. Since the deposit is not credited by the bank the pass book overdraft is 5000 plus 1500 which equals 6500.
explanation: An uncredited deposit increases the overdraft balance in the pass book.

text: A business bought goods worth 40000 with a trade discount of ten percent. The amount to be recorded in the purchases book is
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Trade discount is deducted before recording so 40000 minus ten percent equals 36000.

text: The balance of the trading account that shows excess of expenses over income from operations is a gross
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: When the debit side of the trading account exceeds the credit side the result is a gross loss.

text: Bad debts written off are shown in the profit and loss account as a loss
subject: Financial Accounting
explanation: Bad debts are irrecoverable amounts and are treated as a loss in the profit and loss account.

text: Explain the limitations of single entry system of accounting
subject: Financial Accounting
correctAnswer: Single entry does not provide a complete double entry record so a true and fair view is not possible. A trial balance cannot be prepared and errors and fraud are hard to detect. It is difficult to value assets and compute accurate profit.
explanation: Cover absence of trial balance difficulty of detection and unreliable profit figures.
